reconstructed_theorem_text:
For arbitrary natural numbers n and N, put E=R^(n+1) with its Euclidean inner product, S={z in E: ||z||=1}, and C=S^(Fin N). No positivity hypothesis on n or N is present. C carries the product of the sphere charted-space instances displayed in the compiler output, with source model sphereProductModel n N = product_i R^n. In the regularity conditions below, C^k means precisely ContMDiff of order k for this source model and the self model on the indicated real vector-space target.

The integration measure is fixed by the following definitions. Write H=homeomorphUnitSphereProd E, a homeomorphism E\{0} -> S x (0,infinity). The supplied characterization identifies its first component as z/||z||. Let sigma=volume.toSphere on S, literally
 sigma = (n+1) * first_marginal( (comap(g,volume_E)) restricted to S x {r in (0,infinity): r<1} ),
where g=Subtype.val composed with H inverse and the displayed scalar denotes scaling of a measure. Let mu_1=sigma(S)^(-1) * sigma, with the inverse and scalar multiplication in the extended nonnegative reals as in the supplied definition, and let mu be the Fin N product of mu_1. This is the exact normalized polar angular-measure construction in the packet. No separate arbitrary measure or density is a theorem parameter.

For x in C, i in Fin N and y in S, x[i<-y] means replacing only the ith coordinate of x by y. For a scalar or E-valued function a on S define its literal radial extension R(a):E -> target by
 R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) if z!=0, and R(a)(0)=0.
The zero value is part of the definition, not a smoothness assertion at the origin.

For a real function u on C define the ith vector G_i u(x) as follows. Set u_(i,x)(y)=u(x[i<-y]). Take the real ambient gradient of R(u_(i,x)) at the ambient vector x_i, and orthogonally project it onto (R x_i)^perp:
 G_i u(x)=P_(x_i) grad_E R(u_(i,x))(x_i),
 P_(x_i) a = a-<x_i,a>x_i.
Here the ambient gradient is literally the inverse Riesz map applied to fderiv_R. The supplied projection characterizations justify the displayed P formula and its values in x_i^perp.

For a family W_i:C -> E define
 Div W(x)=sum_(i in Fin N) sum_(k in Fin(n+1))
   lineDeriv_R [z -> (R(y -> W_i(x[i<-y]))(z))_k] (x_i) e_k,
where e_k is the kth standard Euclidean basis vector. Thus each component field is radially extended in its own sphere coordinate while the other configuration coordinates are held fixed. The supplied coordinate-divergence theorem identifies the inner sum with the diagonal trace sum of the Frechet derivative when that ambient extension is differentiable at x_i. These G_i and Div are exactly the defined sphereProductGradient and sphereProductDivergence operators; no independent intrinsic Riemannian, covariant-divergence, Hausdorff-measure or Wasserstein API identification is substituted for these definitions.

Let f,rho,g:C -> R be arbitrary. Assume f and rho are C^1 and g is C^2 for the specified product sphere model. Define, rather than independently quantify over, the family
 V_i(x)=rho(x) G_i g(x).
No nonnegativity, strict positivity, normalization, probability-density interpretation or nonvanishing assumption on rho is present.

Then all three real functions
 x -> Div V(x),
 x -> f(x) Div V(x),
 x -> rho(x) sum_i <G_i f(x),G_i g(x)>
are integrable with respect to mu. In addition,
 integral_C Div V dmu=0,
 integral_C f Div V dmu
   = - integral_C rho(x) sum_i <G_i f(x),G_i g(x)> dmu(x).

On the left, Div acts on the entire field x -> rho(x)G_i g(x); it is not defined here as rho times Div(Gg). The theorem does not separately state a Laplacian/product-rule expansion. No separate tangency or C^1 hypothesis on V is supplied: V is fixed by the given formula. The measure of integration remains mu; it is not changed to a measure with density rho. Integrability is a conclusion, not a premise. All sums run over every i in Fin N with no factor 1/N, and all inner products are the real Euclidean inner product on E. The scalar fields are actual pointwise functions, not Lp equivalence classes. There is no temporal domain, horizon, limiting mode, existential constant or hidden quantitative bound. The quantifier order is forall n,N, forall f,rho,g, then C^1(f), C^1(rho), C^2(g), then the local definition of V and the five simultaneous conclusions.
objects: Arbitrary scalar f,rho,g:C->R; the locally defined vector family V_i(x)=rho(x)G_i g(x); the same fixed normalized angular product measure mu, radial component gradients and literal product coordinate divergence.
domains: n,N are arbitrary natural numbers, including zero. E=R^(n+1), S={z:||z||=1}, C=Fin N -> S; i ranges over Fin N, ambient coordinate k over Fin(n+1). Scalar values and integral identities are real. C uses the instantiated product sphere charts and inherited Borel product measurable space. Every integral is over all C with mu=the finite product of normalized volume.toSphere.
quantifiers: For every n,N in Nat and every f,rho,g:C->R: C^1(f) implies C^1(rho) implies C^2(g); then let V_i(x)=rho(x)G_i g(x), and assert the conjunction of the three integrabilities and two integral equalities. V is not independently universally or existentially quantified.
assumptions: Exactly C^1(f), C^1(rho) and C^2(g) for the supplied manifold model. No positivity, normalization, probability-density interpretation or nonvanishing of rho. No separate regularity/tangency assumption on V, and no integrability premise. There is no n>0 or N>0 hypothesis.
conclusion: With V_i=rho*G_i g: Integrable_mu(Div V), Integrable_mu(f*Div V), Integrable_mu(x -> rho(x)*sum_i <G_i f(x),G_i g(x)>), integral_mu Div V=0, and integral_mu f Div V = - integral_mu rho*sum_i <G_i f,G_i g>.
scopes: Global manifold regularity for the specified product source model. Operators and input functions are pointwise, with no quotient/representative choice. Integrable means real Bochner/Lebesgue L1 integrability, including the measurability and finite-norm-integral requirement, with respect to the exact mu. Conclusions include all three integrabilities and two scalar equalities. No time parameter, horizon, a.e. derivative, convergence or asymptotic statement occurs. rho multiplies the defined vector field before differentiation on the left. On the right it multiplies the entire finite inner-product sum. Every integral uses mu, not a rho-weighted replacement measure; rho may be signed.
constant_dependencies: No existential constant or estimate. Unit radius is exactly 1. Ambient dimension is n+1, factor model dimension n, and there are N sphere factors. Sum over factors is not divided by N. The fixed measure scaling is the ENNReal inverse of sigma(S), with sigma=volume.toSphere and its printed finrank scaling; it is not an arbitrary or function-dependent parameter. The sign in the integration-by-parts equality is exactly minus.

definition_reconstruction.ambient: SphereAmbient n is EuclideanSpace R (Fin(n+1)), itself PiLp 2 of real coordinates, with the displayed real Euclidean inner product.
definition_reconstruction.sphere: SpherePoint n is the literal metric unit sphere centered at zero, treated as a subtype.
definition_reconstruction.configuration: SphereConfiguration n N is Fin N -> S with product topology, product of inherited Borel measurable structures and the displayed product sphere charted-space instance.
definition_reconstruction.regularity_model: sphereProductModel n N is ModelWithCorners.pi of the R^n models. The actual ContMDiff parameters use piChartedSpace with instChartedSpaceEuclideanSpaceRealFinElemHAddNatOfNatSphere n; targets use their self chart/model. Orders 1 and 2 are exact.
definition_reconstruction.measure: sigma=volume.toSphere; its printed body is finrank_R(E) times the first marginal of comap(Subtype.val o H^-1,volume), restricted to S x {r>0:r<1}, H=homeomorphUnitSphereProd E. mu_1=sigma(S)^-1 smul sigma in ENNReal, mu=Measure.pi (fun i:Fin N => mu_1). Product-measure rectangle and total-mass characterizations are supplied.
definition_reconstruction.radial_extension: R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) away from zero and R(a)(0)=0, using the supplied H first-component theorem.
definition_reconstruction.tangent_projection: starProjection onto (R x_i)^perp is ambient a -> a-<x_i,a>x_i because ||x_i||=1.
definition_reconstruction.component_gradient: G_i u(x)=P_(x_i) gradient_R R(y -> u(update x i y))(x_i).
definition_reconstruction.coordinate_divergence: coordinateDivergence A(z)=sum_k lineDeriv_R (y -> (A y)_k) z e_k. Its equality to sum_k (fderiv_R A(z)e_k)_k is supplied conditional on DifferentiableAt.
definition_reconstruction.product_divergence: Div W(x)=sum_i coordinateDivergence R(y -> W_i(update x i y))(x_i).
definition_reconstruction.update: update x i y has value y at i and agrees with x at every other coordinate.
definition_reconstruction.local_V: V_i(x)=rho(x) smul G_i g(x), with scalar multiplication in the actual real Euclidean ambient space.

Radial extension has an explicit zero value at the ambient origin; all gradient/divergence evaluations in the target occur at unit vectors. No smoothness at zero or replacement of a total derivative operator by an unproved characterization is added.
